correctness.rationale: Vanishing of the cubic coefficients gives W^(2)=W^perp for the bilinear coordinate pairing, hence W^(4)=W and descent to F4. The restricted normal derivative sending a complementary vector n to sum_i (r_i^(2)·n)t_i² is an isomorphism onto the three-dimensional square span; the resulting products t_i²t_j are distinct, so the plane Hilbert tangent vanishes. Over F4, a weight-two vector splits off a self-dual two-coordinate summand, and a residual length-four self-dual space in systematic form has monomial 2×2 right block (each row has odd weight). Without weight two, the 3×3 right block in systematic form has three full rows. Normalize its first row and first column to one; orthogonality forces the other rows to be (1,α,α²) and (1,α²,α), in either order. Thus the two types are each one monomial orbit. Independent replay built systematic planes from all orthogonal norm-one triples, deduplicated by projective point sets and compared all ordered intersections by cardinality 0,1,5,21 instead of rank. It confirmed counts 405 and 486, both weight profiles, all three quotient matrices and the 15 Frobenius fixed planes, all in the pairing class. The remaining Frobenius cycles are pairs and give the stated zeta function. The quotient eigenvalues follow from each row sum and the trace.
residual_risks: The strata are coordinate-monomial, not unitary invariants. The finite replay verifies exact finite data; descent and étaleness use the separate algebraic argument.

value.rationale: Coordinate structure gives a natural partition of the maximal isotropic spaces into the familiar pairing family and the characteristic-two hexacode family. The complete equitable quotient for each of the three intersection relations resolves where the global valencies go under this geometrically meaningful symmetry restriction. It supplies usable coordinate-sensitive incidence data rather than a recount of 891 or a list of code weights.
residual_risks: Value is for the exact embedded fourfold and distinguished coordinates, not a new description of all unitary incidences or a general cubic-fourfold theorem.
